# python-llm-30
30 Day Challenge to Refresh on Python and LLMs

*PLAN GENERATED BY CLAUDE*

Weeks 1-2: Python Foundations (Days 1-14)
	•	Days 1-7: Set up Python 3.12+, an editor, a virtual environment, and Git. Cover core data types, control flow, functions, comprehensions, file I/O, and exceptions. Week 1 mini project: a command-line tool that works on a CSV or JSON file of fake customer records.
	•	Days 8-14: Classes and dataclasses, iterators and generators, decorators, type hints, and the standard library (collections, itertools, pathlib, json, argparse). Week 2 mini project: refactor your Week 1 tool into a small scanner that flags column names and patterns that look like PII.
	•	Ongoing practice: 2-3 easy problems a day on Exercism's Python track.
Week 3: Python for Data and First LLM Calls (Days 15-21)
	•	Day 15: pytest and project structure.
	•	Day 16: pandas basics and sqlite3, since you'll use them with LLMs constantly.
	•	Day 17: Your first LLM API calls with the Anthropic Python SDK: messages, system prompts, temperature, and streaming. Use the docs at docs.claude.com.
	•	Day 18: Structured outputs: getting reliable JSON back, validating it with pydantic, and handling failures and retries.
	•	Day 19: Tool use (function calling), where the model decides to call your Python functions.
	•	Day 20: Prompting techniques that matter in practice: few-shot examples, clear task framing, and handling long context.
	•	Day 21: Mini project: send column names and sample values to an LLM and have it classify the sensitivity of each column (PII, financial, public), returning validated JSON.
Week 4: Capstone (Days 22-30)
Pick one capstone and build it end to end, with tests, a README, and a short demo.
Days 22-30 breakdown
	•	Days 22-23: Learn embeddings, chunking strategies, and a vector store, plus the basics of RAG.
	•	Days 24-28: Build the capstone, committing to GitHub daily.
	•	Day 29: Add evals, error handling, logging, and a README section on limitations and governance considerations (data privacy, prompt injection, hallucinations).
	•	Day 30: Record a 3-5 minute demo and write a short blog post or LinkedIn post about what you built.
